newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's Statoil posts record operating profit.
newsitem.headline: Norway's Statoil posts record operating profit.

text.p: Norwegian state oil company Den Norske Stats Oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said Thursday it achieved record operating profits in 1996 thanks to higher crude prices, increased production and stable operations.

The company posted operating profits of 18.2 billion crowns ($2.67 billion), a rise of 34 percent from 13.6 billion crowns ($1.99 billion) in 1995. However, net profits were steady at 5.3 billion crowns ($779 million). The company said it has an operating profit target of 25 billion crowns ($3.67 billion) by 2000.

Statoil said the steady after-tax profit was because a significant share of revenues came from offshore operations -- which attract far higher tax than land-based activities -- while less-taxed petrochemicals showed a decline in earnings.
